questions.rationale: The objective is a single verifiable fact — the existence of a specific christening event in Triesen, Liechtenstein. Catholic parish registers for Triesen survive and are accessible through FamilySearch digitized collections covering the 18th century, making a direct record search the appropriate first step. No prior research exists on this question.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: independent_verification blocks: only one source was accessed — the FamilySearch derivative index (collection 1708589 / src_001). The original Triesen Kirchenbuch (FHL #115845), which is the highest-reliability primary source for this event, was not examined because it is microfilm-only and not accessible via online tools in this session. Without the original, three criteria fail: (1) original_substitution — the derivative index was not replaced with the original Kirchenbuch image; (2) independent_verification — no second independent source corroborates the christening, as the Familienbücher search returned nil and no indexed marriage record was found; (3) overturn_risk — elevated because an index transcription error cannot be ruled out without seeing the original register. The Kirchenbuch is accessible at a FamilySearch Center or via microfilm order and is not sealed by privacy law; the inaccessibility exception does not apply. Research must be extended to obtain and examine FHL #115845 before exhaustiveness can be declared.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Substantially yes — the FamilySearch derivative index (collection 1708589) returns an exact match: Magdalena Schedler, christened 12 Jun 1743, Triesen, Liechtenstein, father Joannes Schedler, mother Catharina Schedlerin. The match directly answers the question. However, the answer rests on a single derivative source; it is not yet a proved conclusion.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: The only indexed online collection for Liechtenstein christenings (FS 1708589) was searched and returned a positive hit. Ancestry's equivalent collection (9913) is confirmed as the same underlying index and was correctly skipped. The Familienbücher (FHL #103425) and indexed marriage registers were searched with nil results. The critical gap is the original Triesen Kirchenbuch (FHL #115845), which is the definitive baptism register for 1743 and covers this event. It is microfilm-only, undigitized, and not accessible via online tools — but it is accessible at a FamilySearch Center. FAN research was not applicable: the event is directly recorded in the christening register. Civil registration did not begin in Liechtenstein until 1878 (births/marriages/deaths) per the FamilySearch wiki; the 1743 event falls entirely outside civil registration.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Not met. The derivative index (collection 1708589) was accessed but the original Kirchenbuch image from FHL microfilm #115845 was not. volume_search returned 0 results and the image ARK returned an error, confirming the images are not online. The original is accessible via a FamilySearch Center visit or microfilm order. Until the original baptism register entry is read, this criterion is not satisfied.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Not met. Only one source unit was accessed: the FamilySearch derivative index (src_001), itself derived from the Kirchenbuch. The Familienbücher search (pli_004) was negative — no indexed family register for Schedler exists on FamilySearch. The marriage register search (pli_005) found no indexed record for Joannes Schedler × Catharina Gosnerin. No second independent source corroborates the christening. At least two independent sources with different informants or institutional origins are required.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Borderline. The information extracted is classified as primary — the officiating priest recorded the christening firsthand, and the parents supplied the child's name at time of christening. However, the record accessed is the derivative index, not the original register. Strictly, at least one original record must be in hand; the index is a proxy. The original Kirchenbuch (if examined) would satisfy this criterion as an original record with primary information.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No conflicts are recorded for q_001. The only apparent discrepancy — mother named as 'Catharina Schedlerin' in the index vs. 'Catharina Gosnerin' (birth surname) in the tree — was analyzed and resolved as a standard German/Alemannic feminine-suffix convention (Schedlerin = wife of Schedler). No contradicting evidence exists.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Elevated. The derivative index is drawn from a Legacy (incomplete) collection covering approximately 50% of pre-1800 Liechtenstein records. Index transcription errors are a known risk. Without examining the original Kirchenbuch entry, there is a non-hypothetical possibility that the date, parents' names, or child's name could differ from what the index reports. Once the original is examined and confirms the index entry, overturn risk drops to low — no other record type known to this jurisdiction and period could plausibly name different parents for this child.

items.rationale: FamilySearch collection 1708589 ('Liechtenstein, Births and Baptisms, 1650-1875') is the only online indexed source for Liechtenstein baptisms in this period. Search for child name 'Magdalena' with parents 'Joannes Schedler' (also try Schödler) and 'Catharina Gosnerin' (also try Gosner, Gösner) around 1743. The collection is a Legacy (incomplete) index — ~468 records indexed for all of Liechtenstein 1700-1750 — so a miss does not prove absence; the original Kirchenbuch must then be checked. A hit must be verified against the original image.

The definitive primary source is the Triesen Catholic Kirchenbuch, 1638-1916 (FamilySearch catalog #115845). It covers the 1743 target date and records: child name, date/place of baptism, parents' names, godparents. volume_search returns 0 results for Liechtenstein 1700-1760, so images may not be online yet — access through the FamilySearch catalog page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/115845) or at a FamilySearch Center. Records are in Latin; use the Latin Genealogical Word List. This is the highest-reliability source for the question.

Ancestry.com collection 9913 ('Liechtenstein, Births and Baptisms, 1650-1875') uses the same underlying index as FamilySearch collection 1708589 but may expose different search options or additional derivative records. Subscription required. Search the same name variants (Magdalena Schedler/Schödler, parents Joannes and Catharina Gosnerin/Gosner). Fallback if pli_001 returns nothing, to confirm the FamilySearch result (or lack thereof) before moving to microfilm.

Familienbücher (family registers), Triesen Standesamt, 1794-1956 (FamilySearch catalog #103425). Although this series begins in 1794, family registers routinely contain retrospective household data for families already resident in the parish — a Schedler family entry may list Magdalena as a child with her 1743 christening date. This is the FAN/household item: a family register places all children of Joannes Schedler and Catharina Gosnerin in one record, potentially confirming or denying Magdalena's existence as their daughter. The date range reflects when the register was maintained, not when Magdalena lived.

Search the Triesen Kirchenbuch marriage registers (catalog #115845, 1638-1916) for the marriage of Joannes Schedler and Catharina Gosnerin, estimated 1720-1743 (they must have married before the 1743 christening). A marriage record establishes the couple as a unit resident in Triesen before 1743, corroborating the premise of the question, and may supply Catharina's maiden name or parents, aiding any further research. Also try spelling variants. Access same as pli_002 — catalog page or FamilySearch Center.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Christening of Magdalena Schedler, Daughter of Joannes Schedler and Catharina Gosnerin, Triesen, Liechtenstein, 12 June 1743

### Research Question

Did Catharina Gosnerin and Joannes Schedler of Triesen, Liechtenstein have a daughter Magdalena, christened 12 June 1743?

### Conclusion

The evidence strongly suggests that Magdalena Schedler, christened 12 June 1743 at Triesen, Liechtenstein, was the daughter of Joannes Schedler and his wife Catharina Gosnerin (recorded in the christening register under the married-name form Catharina Schedlerin). This conclusion rests at the **probable** tier: the evidence is direct and the information primary, but it derives from a single derivative index entry rather than the examined original parish register.

### Source and Evidence Analysis

The sole source for this conclusion is an index entry in the FamilySearch collection "Liechtenstein Geburten und Taufen 1650-1875" (collection 1708589, Legacy Collection), citing the Triesen Kirchenbuch as its underlying original: "Liechtenstein Geburten und Taufen 1650-1875," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:MPKY-HNJ : 7 February 2020), Eintrag für Magdalena Schedler; citing baptism Triesen, Liechtenstein; FHL microfilm.

This source is **derivative**: it is an index drawn from FHL microfilm of the Triesen Kirchenbuch (catalog #115845), not the original register itself. The index has known limitations — FamilySearch acknowledges collection 1708589 is a Legacy Collection with incomplete coverage of Liechtenstein records, estimated at approximately 50% before 1800. Transcription errors cannot be excluded without examining the original.

The information in the index is **primary** for the christening event itself: the officiating priest personally performed and recorded the baptism, making him a firsthand witness for the date (12 June 1743) and place (Triesen, Liechtenstein). The child's name (Magdalena Schedler) and the parents' identities (Joannes Schedler as father; Catharina Schedlerin as mother) were supplied by the presenting parents at the time of the christening — household members present at the event, making their statements primary information as well.

The evidence is **direct**: the index entry explicitly names both parents in the context of this child's christening, answering the research question without requiring inference.

### Identity Correlation

**Magdalena Schedler (child):** The record's christening persona — Magdalena Schedler, Female, christened 12 Jun 1743, Triesen, Liechtenstein — was linked to tree stub I1 (Magdalena Schedler, Female). The stub was created from this record and has no independent corroboration; the link is rated probable (pe_001–pe_003).

**Joannes Schedler (father):** The record's father persona — Joannes Schedler, Male — was linked to tree person K4K8-5K3 (Joannes Schedler, Male) at confident confidence (pe_004–pe_006). The given name and surname match exactly, and the record's father occupies precisely the position K4K8-5K3 holds in the family tree: father of a child born to this couple at Triesen in the 1740s. Corroboration comes from the tree's existing ParentChild links for three other Schedler children (Antonius, Josephus, and Rosa) drawn from adjacent entries in the same christening collection, all naming Joannes Schedler and Catharina Gosnerin/Schedlerin as parents at Triesen.

**Catharina Gosnerin / Schedlerin (mother):** The record gives the mother's name as Catharina Schedlerin. This is the standard German and Alemannic convention whereby a wife adopts the feminine inflected form of her husband's surname: Schedler (husband) → Schedlerin (wife). Her birth surname, Gosner/Gosnerin, does not appear in this record; it is known from tree context. The given name Catharina matches exactly, and the position — mother of a child of Joannes Schedler at Triesen — matches tree person KZS8-RS7 (Catharina Gosnerin, Female) precisely. The name discrepancy is fully accounted for by the naming convention and is not a conflict. The link was rated confident (pe_008–pe_010).

### Conflicts

No conflicts are recorded for this question. The only apparent discrepancy — the mother appearing as Schedlerin in the christening record rather than Gosnerin — was analyzed above and is fully resolved by the German/Alemannic feminine-suffix convention.

### Scope of Research and Limitations

The FamilySearch derivative index (collection 1708589), the only indexed online collection for Liechtenstein christenings, was searched and returned the positive result above. The Familienbücher (FHL #103425) and indexed marriage registers were searched with nil results for the Schedler family. Civil registration did not commence in Liechtenstein until 1878; no civil records apply to a 1743 christening.

The critical gap is the **original Triesen Kirchenbuch** (FHL microfilm #115845), which covers this event and is the highest-reliability source available. It is microfilm-only and not accessible via online tools; it can be consulted at a FamilySearch Center or via microfilm order. Examination of the original register would: (1) confirm or correct the index transcription; (2) supply an original record with primary information, satisfying the GPS original-substitution criterion; and (3) potentially reveal additional details such as godparents. Until the original is examined and independently corroborates the index, the conclusion remains at **probable** rather than **proved**.

No contradicting evidence was encountered in any searched repository.

### Tier Declaration

The evidence strongly suggests that Magdalena Schedler, christened 12 June 1743 at Triesen, Liechtenstein, is the daughter of Joannes Schedler (K4K8-5K3) and Catharina Gosnerin (KZS8-RS7). The conclusion is **probable**: the direct, primary-information evidence from the christening index points clearly and without contradiction to this parentage, but one GPS component is incomplete — the original parish register (FHL #115845) has not been examined to substitute for the derivative index or to provide independent verification. To advance this conclusion to **proved**, a researcher should obtain and examine the original Triesen Kirchenbuch entry at a FamilySearch Center or via microfilm order.

localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Triesen, Liechtenstein (1740s)

## Jurisdiction & Background

Triesen is a municipality in the southern Principality of Liechtenstein, bordered by Austria (Vorarlberg) to the east and Switzerland (Graubünden/St. Gallen) to the west. In 1743 Liechtenstein was a principality within the Holy Roman Empire; it became fully sovereign in 1806. No boundary changes affected Triesen's ecclesiastical jurisdiction for this period. Records are organised at the local municipality (Gemeinde) level. Population of all Liechtenstein c.1800: ~5,802 (country-level Gapminder estimate).

## Primary Source for 1743: Catholic Church Records

Civil registration did not begin until **1878** (births/marriages/deaths) and **1789** (family registers) — both postdate the 1743 christening. The sole contemporary source is the **Catholic parish register**.

| Record Set | Coverage | Access | Digitisation Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Triesen Kirchenbuch, 1638–1916 | Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations | FS catalog #115845 — microfilmed; volume_search returned 0 results; may require FamilySearch Center | Browse-only (microfilm) |
| Liechtenstein, Births & Baptisms, 1650–1875 (FS coll. 1708589) | Country-wide partial index | Free at FamilySearch; also Ancestry ($), MyHeritage ($), Findmypast ($) | Partial index + images — Legacy Collection |

**Critical caveat:** Collection 1708589 is a Legacy Collection — incomplete for every place and time period. FamilySearch has ~468 indexed birth records for all of Liechtenstein 1700–1750. A hit must be verified against the original; a miss does not prove absence.

## Other Record Types

- Familienbücher (Family Registers), Triesen Standesamt, 1794–1956 — FS catalog #103425, microfilm. Begins 1794; may contain retrospective family data but 1743 predates this series.
- Liechtenstein State Archives (Landesarchiv, Vaduz) — court, land, and probate records; no 18th-century online access.
- Historischer Verein für das Fürstentum Liechtenstein: https://www.lub.li/

## Key Quirks

1. Index is incomplete — a miss is not proof of absence; always check the original Kirchenbuch.
2. Kirchenbuch (1638–1916) appears microfilm-only; may require a FamilySearch Center visit.
3. Records written in Latin (Catholic); German Genealogical Word List and Latin Genealogical Word List essential.
4. Population coverage ~50% before 1800 — significant gaps in the indexed portion.
5. Triesen borders Austria (Vorarlberg) and Switzerland — search neighboring parishes if Triesen records are silent.
